taj_mahal.name: Taj Mahal
taj_mahal.description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river, recognized worldwide as a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
historical_details: Commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his favorite wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Chief architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahori; construction completed around 1648-1653.
Design incorporates symmetrical gardens (charbagh), a grand central dome surrounded by four smaller chattris, and four free-standing minarets tilted slightly outward.
Designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
taj_mahal.architectural_style: Mughal Architecture (Islamic, Persian, and Indian synthesis)

qutub_minar.name: Qutub Minar
qutub_minar.description: A 72.5-meter tall minaret constructed of red sandstone and marble, forming part of the UNESCO Qutub complex.
historical_details: Construction initiated by Qutb-ud-din Aibak around 1199 CE to commemorate victory and serve as a minaret for the adjacent Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
Subsequent storeys added by his successor Shams-ud-din Iltutmish, and later repaired by Firuz Shah Tughlaq after lightning strikes.
Features distinctive fluted cylindrical and angular stone shafts adorned with Nagari and Arabic calligraphic inscriptions.
Contains 379 spiral staircase steps leading through five tapering storeys with cantilevered balconies.

red_fort.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
red_fort.description: A historic fort complex enclosed by massive red sandstone defensive walls, serving as the ceremonial residence of Mughal emperors for nearly two centuries.
historical_details: Commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638 when deciding to shift his capital from Agra to Delhi (Shahjahanabad).
Designed by architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori, blending Timurid, Persian, and Hindu architectural traditions.
Home to famous structures such as the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), and Lahori Gate.
The Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the Lahori Gate every Independence Day (August 15).

india_gate.name: India Gate
india_gate.description: A 42-meter high triumphal arch war memorial honoring 84,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army who died between 1914 and 1921.
historical_details: Designed by British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens, inspired by the Arch of Constantine in Rome and Arc de Triomphe in Paris.
Foundation stone laid in February 1921 by the Duke of Connaught; inaugurated in February 1931 by Viceroy Lord Irwin.
Inscribed with the names of over 13,300 servicemen on its pale red and yellow Bharatpur sandstone surfaces.
The Amar Jawan Jyoti (Flame of the Immortal Soldier) beneath the arch commemorated fallen soldiers since 1971.

charminar.name: Charminar
charminar.description: A square monument and mosque built in 1591 with four ornate 48.7-meter minarets, serving as the iconic symbol of Hyderabad.
historical_details: Constructed by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, to commemorate the end of a devastating plague in the city.
Located at the intersection of the historical trade route connecting Golconda fort with the port city of Machilipatnam.
Structure features four grand arches facing the cardinal directions, each supporting a 4-storey minaret with double carved balconies.
The top floor houses the oldest surviving mosque in Hyderabad.
charminar.architectural_style: Indo-Islamic (Qutb Shahi with Persian & Hindu accents)

hawa_mahal.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
hawa_mahal.description: A five-storey pink and red sandstone palace renowned for its honeycomb facade with 953 finely carved jharokhas (small casements).
historical_details: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh and designed by Lal Chand Ustad.
Designed in the form of the crown of Lord Krishna, to whom the Maharaja was devoted.
The 953 screened windows allowed royal women to observe street festivals without being seen from outside (Purdah tradition).
Engineered with natural venturi air cooling principles, giving it the name 'Palace of Winds' due to cool breezes circulating through the chambers.
hawa_mahal.architectural_style: Rajput Architecture (blend of Hindu Rajput and Islamic Mughal)
